verdict.rationale: uv lets you pin automation environments reproducibly: `uv.lock` records exact dependency information, scripts carry inline dependency metadata that `uv add --script` updates, and tools can be run at specific versions such as `uvx ruff@0.6.0`. These are plain-text artifacts you can commit, review and revert, but uv itself offers no native history, review or rollback feature, so those steps depend on external source control. missing for 10: built-in automation version history, a review/diff workflow, a first-class rollback command, and hands-on evidence of lockfile-based rollback.
